title: AlloyDB blocking session
match_key: blocking_session pg_locks lock_wait blocking backend pg_stat_activity
body: A Postgres backend is confirmed holding a lock that is blocking other sessions, identified via pg_stat_activity / pg_locks (alloydb_find_blocking_session). Terminate exactly that backend -- SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) -- using the pid returned by the lookup, never a guessed value, to release everything waiting behind it.

title: AlloyDB runaway query
match_key: runaway_query long_running query_duration high cpu backend
body: A single query has been running far longer than expected, consuming excessive CPU/IO on its backend. Terminate that backend directly -- SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) -- same underlying mechanism as alloydb_kill_blocking_session, kept as a separate allowlisted action so it is audited and reasoned about under its own name.

title: AlloyDB idle-in-transaction buildup
body: Backends have been sitting idle-in-transaction past a safe threshold (300s in the reference config), holding locks and connection slots for no active work. Batch-terminate every matching backend -- SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'idle in transaction' AND state_change < now() - interval '{idle_seconds} seconds'. Auto-executes at Tier 2: allowed without human approval, but every run is logged loudly to the audit trail -- can affect multiple sessions at once, broader blast radius than a Tier 1 single-backend kill.

title: AlloyDB connection storm
match_key: AlloyDB connection storm -- last-resort reset requested
body: Last-resort, instance-wide reset: terminates every other active session on the database -- SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE pid <> pg_backend_pid() AND datname = current_database(). Requires human approval via Slack before it ever runs (Tier 3) -- approving it during a live demo genuinely terminates every other session, so only approve this in a controlled setting.
